## Code Review: `tools/bench-agent-cost/fixtures/review_target.py`

### Critical (blocks merge)

| # | File:Line | Category | Principle | Issue | Fix |
|---|-----------|----------|-----------|-------|-----|
| 1 | `review_target.py:11,24` | Security — SQL injection | OWASP Top 10 (Injection); coding-standards.md §3.2 (validate at boundaries, use safe idioms) | `order_id` is interpolated directly into the SQL string via an f-string in both the `SELECT` and the `UPDATE`. Any caller passing a non-sanitized `order_id` can inject arbitrary SQL. | Use parameterized queries: `db_conn.execute("SELECT total FROM orders WHERE id = ?", (order_id,))` (or the driver's placeholder syntax). |
| 2 | `review_target.py:19-22` | Anti-pattern — swallowed error | coding-standards.md §9 ("Catching / swallowing errors 'just in case' without a named failure mode"); §3.2 (handle errors at the appropriate layer) | On a non-200 payment response the function silently returns `None`. The caller cannot distinguish "payment declined," "gateway timeout," and "success with $0 total" — all collapse to `None`. No failure mode is named or raised. | Raise a domain-specific exception (e.g., `PaymentFailedError(order_id, resp.status_code)`) or return a typed `Result`/`PaymentOutcome` object that the caller can pattern-match on, instead of an ambiguous sentinel. |

### Important (should fix before merge)

| # | File:Line | Category | Principle | Issue | Fix |
|---|-----------|----------|-----------|-------|-----|
| 3 | `review_target.py:8-25` | SOLID — SRP | coding-standards.md §1.1 (one reason to change); §2.1 (Core/Domain must have zero I/O) | `process_order` mixes three concerns with independent reasons to change: reading order data (persistence), applying a discount (business rule), and charging a payment gateway (infrastructure I/O). A change to the discount policy, the DB schema, or the payment provider each force an edit to this one function. Description requires an "and." | Split into: a pure `apply_discount(total: float) -> float` (core/domain, no I/O), an `OrderRepository` port for the DB reads/writes, and a `PaymentGateway` port for the charge call. `process_order` becomes an orchestrating use case that composes the three via injected dependencies. |
| 4 | `review_target.py:8` (params `order_id`, `db_conn`) / whole function | SOLID — DIP; Clean Architecture layering | coding-standards.md §1.5 (core must not depend on low-level modules); §2.2 (dependency rule); §5.1 (reverse DI — core declares interfaces, not concrete infra) | The function takes a concrete `db_conn` and calls the concrete `requests` module directly — there is no abstraction (`PaymentGateway`, `OrderRepository` protocol) between the business logic and the infrastructure. This is a direct infrastructure→core layer violation: the "core" logic (discount calc) is welded to a DB connection object and a hard-coded HTTP client. | Declare `PaymentGateway` and `OrderRepository` protocols in the domain layer; inject concrete adapters (`RequestsPaymentGateway`, `SqlOrderRepository`) at a composition root. `process_order` depends only on the protocols. |
| 5 | `review_target.py:13` | Coding standard — no magic numbers / no invented constants | coding-standards.md §3.1 ("No magic numbers. Every numeric constant has a name or a source comment"); §8 ("No invented constants... every hardcoded number must have a source") | `500` (discount threshold) and `0.9` (10% discount multiplier) are bare literals with no name and no `# source:` citation tracing them to a documented business rule. | Extract named constants, e.g. `BULK_ORDER_DISCOUNT_THRESHOLD = 500  # source: pricing policy doc §4.2` and `BULK_ORDER_DISCOUNT_RATE = 0.9  # source: ...`. |

### Minor (optional, improve later)

| # | File:Line | Category | Principle | Issue | Fix |
|---|-----------|----------|-----------|-------|-----|
| 6 | `review_target.py:8` | Coding standard — type system usage | coding-standards.md §3.2 ("Use the language's type system fully. Type hints... — all of it") | `order_id`, `db_conn`, and the function's return type are untyped. Return type is implicitly `float \| None`, which is not declared anywhere and is easy to misuse at call sites. | Add type hints: `def process_order(order_id: int, order_repo: OrderRepository) -> PaymentOutcome:` (once the DIP fix in finding 4 is applied). |

### Architecture assessment

This file has no layer separation at all — it is a single function acting simultaneously as handler, use case, and infrastructure adapter, in direct violation of the Clean Architecture dependency rule (coding-standards.md §2.2). The two Critical findings (SQL injection, swallowed payment failure) are correctness/security defects that must be fixed regardless of restructuring; the SRP/DIP findings (③, ④) are the structural root cause that made both Critical defects easy to introduce in the first place — inlining raw SQL and an unchecked HTTP call directly into business logic is what a proper `OrderRepository`/`PaymentGateway` boundary would have prevented by construction.
